speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This is part of our social compact, where Singaporeans have access to opportunities and are valued, regardless of their backgrounds or circumstances.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: However, some amongst us may not have sufficient means to provide for themselves and may need additional assistance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Social residential homes provide alternative care arrangements for the most vulnerable amongst us.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: These include seniors, vulnerable adults, children and young persons in need of care and protection, persons with disabilities and destitute persons.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Members in this House may be familiar with some social residential homes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Chen Su Lan Methodist Home, for example, operates a Children’s Home and a Children Disability Home within the same compound.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This home provides residential care to children in need of care and protection, including some with developmental needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: They operate seven social residential homes that provide residential care to children and adults with disabilities, and destitute persons.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Social residential homes have existed in Singapore, long before we gained Independence.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In the past 60 years, we have journeyed with the sector to provide good quality care to residents through funding, licensing and training.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Government first started funding Children’s Homes in the 1960s.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In the 1970s and 1980s, funding was extended to Homes caring for seniors and persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: To improve the quality of care in Homes, we further introduced a licensing regime for Sheltered Homes under the Homes for the Aged Act in 1988, as well as Homes for Children and Young Persons, which include Children’s Homes and Children Disability Homes, under the amendments to the Children and Young Persons Act in 2011.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We also recognised the need to equip their staff with specialised skillsets to care for persons in residential care.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In 2011, MSF and the Social Service Institute developed certificate programmes in residential care.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: To date, about 1,500 professionals have been trained.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: More recently, in 2024, MSF and SG Enable introduced a skills and competency framework to guide Disability Sector Professionals, such as care staff and social workers, in effectively supporting and providing training for persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Over the years, care models have evolved to better meet residents’ needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Today, we adopt a tiered approach for the Children’s Homes, where more intensive care is provided to children with higher care needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Social Residential Homes Bill is a proactive step taken by MSF to codify the good progress that has been made in raising the quality of care provided by the sector over the years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The first question people ask tends to be “Why now?”.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: To be clear, we are not coming from a position of deficit.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Incidents of a serious nature are rare and our Homes are upholding good standards.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The introduction of the Bill is to prepare for the future.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Looking ahead, our population is rapidly ageing and family sizes are shrinking.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Government continues to strengthen efforts to help our seniors age in place, and enable persons with disabilities to live with dignity and participate in the community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Nonetheless, we recognise that there will always be some who are more vulnerable, who will need residential care.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In addition, unlicensed Homes, which are mostly governed today through funding agreements, will now be brought under the ambit of this Bill.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: To arrive at this Bill, we conducted many engagements with the different stakeholders, such as Home operators, board members and members of the public.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Your views, ideas and feedback have helped us to better understand the needs in our social residential home landscape.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Before I go into the key provisions, allow me to first clarify the three main groups of people mentioned in the Bill.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This refers to entities or individuals who are responsible and accountable for the overall compliance with requirements in the Bill.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This refers to individuals who are responsible for strategic leadership and overall management of the Home.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This refers to the head of the Home who oversees day-to-day management of Home operations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: I will now turn to the key provisions of the Bill, which are grouped into three key areas: first, setting clear standards for Homes to deliver quality care; second, establishing stronger safeguards for residents’ safety and well-being; and third, introducing a comprehensive enforcement framework as a deterrence against errant operators.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The first key area is setting clear standards for Homes to deliver quality care.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: MSF will issue Codes of Practice, which comprises regulatory requirements pertaining to key areas, such as: one, governance of the Home; two, management of premises; three, resident management; and four, incident management.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Today, some Homes already comply with standards as set out in our service model requirements, in order to receive funding.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: These Codes of Practice will be issued after close consultation with operators, with guidance and support from MSF to ensure that Homes can meet the specified requirements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The second key area focuses on stronger safeguards for residents’ safety and well-being.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Home residents require 24/7 care and are heavily reliant on others to fulfil daily living needs, such as dressing and toileting.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: It is therefore necessary to ensure that residents not only receive quality care and support, but are also safeguarded from harm in these Homes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Our Home operators share this common commitment with us.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Mr Michael Gan, chief executive officer of the Bishan Home for the Intellectually Disabled, commended the Bill for building on the good foundations our sector has already established.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: He described these clear parameters as a step towards greater accountability to help us achieve our common goal of residents’ safety and well-being.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Ms Nura Binte Hassan, the head of Bukit Batok Home for the Aged, has been part of this sector for more than 10 years, and has seen the progress that we have made over this time.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: She, too, welcomes the Bill as a timely move that provides clarity to the sector and reaffirms our collective commitment towards the welfare and overall well-being of residents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We will put in place measures to ensure residents are not placed at risk of harm in the Home.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This requirement is not new to most of the Home operators.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Today, suitability assessments already apply to staff in our funded Homes, as well as licensees and staff in our licensed Homes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Under the Bill, we will extend this practice to all other Homes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We want to be sure that only individuals with good standing are allowed to be deployed in the Homes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This would ensure continuity of Home operations and continuity of care for residents within.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: In so doing, we can also provide assurance to residents, their family members as well as operators that individuals deployed in these Homes can be trusted to provide quality care to residents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Today, some residents may exhibit aggressive or challenging behaviours due to underlying root causes, such as psychiatric conditions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: These behaviours may put them at risk of harming themselves or others.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Under strictly defined circumstances, the use of reasonable force and/or mechanical restraints by properly trained staff could help to ensure that residents do not further harm themselves, or other persons in the Home, like fellow residents or staff.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We take a firm stance against any unauthorised or excessive use of force or mechanical restraints.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Therefore, MSF will set out the parameters within which the use of force or mechanical restraints would be permitted under the Bill, to deter against any potential forms of abuse.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Board of Visitors comprises professionals who complement MSF’s licensing inspections to ensure that residents reside in safe and sanitary premises.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Board of Visitors visits Homes regularly to check on its premises, speak to residents and provide third-party feedback to MSF on the Home’s living conditions and standards of care.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: They will also share best practices with the Homes they visit.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Today, some Homes, such as Welfare Homes and Children’s Homes, are already visited regularly by a Board of Visitors and have benefited from such visits.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For Marymount Centre, a Children’s Home, these visits have provided a fresh perspective on the Home’s operations and enabled them to identify areas for improvement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For Bukit Batok Home for the Aged, their staff have come to regard such visits as invaluable opportunities for learning of best practices from other Homes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We will therefore extend this good practice to other Homes through this Bill.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The third key area focuses on a comprehensive enforcement framework to deter against errant operators.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: To be clear, our Homes have been providing good care to residents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We have worked well with operators to continuously review the care provided and where needed, made operational adjustments to uphold quality care.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Nonetheless, we do not take for granted that egregious incidents will never happen in our Homes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Under the Bill, MSF may take a range of regulatory action against errant operators.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: As part of a graduated approach to enforcement, we have introduced a range of tools that will allow us to take regulatory actions that correspond to the degree of harm caused.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Regulatory actions under the existing licensing regimes in the Homes for the Aged Act and Children and Young Persons Act are limited.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Today, we can revoke a licence if a regulatory breach has occurred.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: However, some regulatory breaches could be minor and need not warrant a revocation of licence.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Instead, it may be more appropriate to shorten the Home’s licence tenure and allow the Home a chance to rectify the breach.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We are not able to do so today.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: It is therefore timely for MSF to update our suite of regulatory actions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Under the Social Residential Homes Bill, in addition to the revocation of licence, we can also modify, shorten, or suspend licences, and these would be more appropriate for less severe breaches.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: MSF may also pursue criminal penalties for more serious contraventions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Today, residents in our Homes are already protected under other legislation, such as the Children and Young Persons Act, and the Penal Code.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: MSF also closely manages our funded homes through funding agreements, to make sure residents are safe and well.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Under the Social Residential Homes Bill, we have taken the opportunity to review the penalty quanta to be imposed for egregious offences.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For example, under MSF’s Homes for the Aged Act, operating a Sheltered Home without a licence may warrant a fine of no more than $5,000, or imprisonment for no more than two years, or both.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This is the maximum penalty that can be imposed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This signals the importance of the safety and well-being of residents, who are vulnerable.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We recognise that Homes have concerns about the penalties under this Bill.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Many operators in this space are driven by a sense of compassion and a deep sense of social responsibility, and many of their Board members are themselves volunteers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: First and foremost, MSF will take a developmental and supportive stance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Our goal is not to be punitive at the outset, but to support Homes in meeting standards that safeguard the well-being of their residents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We intend to work closely with Homes to uplift the sector.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: To operators of live-in care facilities who are uncertain about their licensing obligations, we encourage you to reach out to MSF for support, as we transition to this new framework.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Further, to assuage Homes’ concerns, we will set out the responsibilities of each stakeholder in our Regulations and Codes of Practice.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Homes will be consulted in this exercise conducted later this year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: As far as possible, MSF will work closely with operators to promptly resolve operational issues.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: However, we recognise that some operators may not be able do so even with other measures, such as capability building and regulatory action, in place.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We must therefore have a fallback plan to minimise disruption and ensure the safety, welfare or well-being of the residents in the Home.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This is when step-in powers will be activated.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This may take the form of appointing a third party to advise the licensee on the Home’s operations or a temporary transfer of residents to another Home.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Should there be a need, MSF may also appoint another operator to temporarily take over operations to ensure continuity of care for residents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: As a start, we will license social residential homes that provide long-term and 24/7 residential care.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Operators whose homes fall under this scope have been consulted and notified of our intent to license the respective Homes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For other operators who are unsure if you fall under the scope of the Bill, please step forward to check with us in MSF.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Should the needs of clients in other Home types evolve, we will review whether to extend the licensing regime to these Homes as well.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Consultations with the relevant stakeholders will be carried out as part of these reviews.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This is on top of ongoing adjustments to our programme funding for social residential homes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: With this funding, Homes will be able to invest in: Training for staff in critical areas such as management of violent behaviours by residents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This will help to keep both residents and staff in our Homes safe.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Updating or installing CCTV systems, to enable Homes to better monitor the safety of residents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This will also function as a deterrent against any form of abuse against residents or staff.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Change management efforts, such as planning and reviewing internal work processes, to adhere to the regulatory requirements under this Bill.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Transition Support Package has been well-received by Home operators.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The components of this package were designed based on operators’ feedback and suggestions on support that would help them transition successfully to the new licensing regime.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: To our Home operators, we are committed to supporting you in this journey.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Besides the Transition Support Package, MSF will also offer developmental consultations to social residential homes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: These developmental consultations form a key part of our pre-implementation preparation.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: They will provide operators with greater clarity on key areas of improvement that they will need to focus on as they prepare to onboard the new licensing regime.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: It will also enable MSF to provide operators with more targeted support and guidance under this Bill.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: I have shared extensively about the enhanced safeguards for residents’ safety and well-being that we will introduce under this Bill.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: I will now touch on what we are doing for the Homes’ staff.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The safety and well-being of staff are equally important to us.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: MSF adopts a zero-tolerance policy towards abuse or harassment of staff.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Any person who abuses staff in the Homes can also be taken to task under the Penal Code 1871.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: Beyond the Bill, MSF and NCSS will continue to work closely with the sector to develop a strong and resilient social service workforce.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: I want to convey my heartfelt appreciation to all staff working in our Homes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: To all the dedicated staff, we want to express our deepest gratitude because we know your work is not easy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The challenges you face require strength, passion and most of all, compassion.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The residents rely on you and your care, and I want to assure you that your contributions are appreciated every single day, even though the residents may not say it.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We recognise that work in the social services can be demanding, which is why we are providing resources to both employers and employees.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: For instance, NCSS works closely with social service agencies to develop stronger organisational capabilities and create a supportive workplace environment.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: The Bill builds upon past efforts by the Government and the social residential home operators to provide good quality care for these residents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: We will continue to work closely with Homes to achieve our collective vision to care for the vulnerable in our society, to realise our ambition for a caring Singapore where no one is left behind.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: First, let us take a moment to appreciate the progress that Singapore has made in establishing a framework of care within our social residential homes.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: These facilities are often staffed with trained and dedicated caregivers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: And many have adopted person-centred care practices that focus on the individual needs, preferences and dignity of their residents.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: However, there is still much work to be done.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Standards of care can vary significantly from one home to another, depending largely on the resources, training and infrastructure of the facility.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: While some residential homes provide exemplary care, others fall short in key areas such as staffing, training and the availability of specialised care for those with dementia, physical disability or other chronic conditions.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: It is therefore vital that we assess and enhance the standards of care in these facilities, confront the myriad challenges they face and prepare for the future demand that will inevitably arise from our changing population demographics.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: One of the more pressing issues is the acute shortage of skilled caregivers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: As our population ages, the demand for caregiving services is expected to increase, yet, we struggle to recruit and retain competent staff.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Low wages, high job demands and difficult working conditions contribute to high turnover rates that would inevitably compromise the quality of care residents receive.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Many homes rely heavily on Government funding, donations and the goodwill of volunteerism.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: As the economic landscape fluctuates, securing the necessary funds to maintain and improve these homes becomes increasingly challenging.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: This precarious financial situation can lead to a detrimental ripple effect on both the quality of care and the emotional well-being of the residents.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: We can expect this growing elderly population to lead to an increased demand for social residential homes.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The complexity of caregiving will escalate, necessitating not only more beds but also more robust support systems that can cater to an ageing population with diverse needs.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: This Bill is, therefore, timely as we proactively address the structure and function of our social residential homes to ensure they can meet both present and future needs and challenges.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Will MSF be making clear the responsibilities and liabilities of the board members of these homes, many of whom are volunteers?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: My concern is that the sharp increase in penalties may result in a chilling effect that deters volunteers from serving on the boards of the social residential homes.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Social residential homes are currently required to comply with sector-specific requirements based on their service models.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: For example, will we see a lower caregiver-to-residents ratio?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: With all homes grappling with a lean workforce, will the new licensing requirements lead to a higher regulatory cost?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: What is the expected increase in costs that MSF projects will be passed down to consumers?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: What are the reasons for excluding them out of the ambit of this regulatory regime?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Are the Boys' and Girls' Homes subject to the same standards as those provided under this Bill?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Who is responsible for ensuring the quality of care at these homes?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: A staff who causes grievous hurt or harm to a resident arising from the use of excessive force or unauthorised forms of restraints can be subjected to criminal penalties under the Penal Code; and regulatory actions under the Act.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: What is reasonable force may differ from person to person and proper training is, therefore, crucial to ensure that the staff assigned to conduct such functions are equipped to do so.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Can MSF share more details about how such cases get picked up for investigation?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Is there a whistle-blowing channel for family members or members of public to report any perceived use of excessive force?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Will there be an ombudsman to investigate such reports?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In the event of MSF taking over or asking another operator to take over a failing facility, how does MSF intend to ensure a smooth transition, especially for the affected staff and the residents involved?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Does MSF have a projection on the number of social residential homes that will be required in the next 10 years?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: What is the projected number of staff needed to operate these homes?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Will MSF consider managing some of these facilities directly, given the amount of resources required?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: We must continue to invest in comprehensive training and continuous professional development for these caregivers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Partnering with educational institutions and industry experts can help equip caregivers with the necessary skills and knowledge to provide exceptional care.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: To retain skilled workers, we must offer competitive salaries, benefits and support systems.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: This Bill aims to codify and harmonise existing standards under a common framework to enable Singaporeans in these homes to benefit from a robust regulatory regime.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Minister Masagos mentioned on 10 March 2025 that MSF has worked closely with social residential homes to raise standards of care for residents and that the new licensing regime is proposed to ensure the safety and wellness of these residents.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: And, if so, what are some of these shortfalls and the reasons behind them?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Second, a licensing regime, while well-intentioned, also involves the meeting of Government-mandated standards in staffing requirements and other service quality matters.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: This will involve both upfront and recurrent costs on the part of social service agencies operating these homes.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Third, staffing requirements are a common concern shared by many social service agencies that manage MSF-funded programmes.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: The resident or client profile of MSF-funded programmes, especially those in residential programmes, is often challenging and complex.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Running a social residential home is also a labour-intensive operation, requiring dedicated staff whose pay often does not commensurate with their work.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Understaffing and staff burnout often lead to poor service and care standards.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: The Minister has also said that this Bill provides for the possibility of homes evolving to meet residents needs where different client profiles could be housed together.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: As I have mentioned earlier about challenging client profiles, may I clarify the rationale behind MSF considering the possibility of housing different client profiles together?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Can the Minister elaborate with some details on this?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: While there could be economies of scale from a bureaucratic perspective; from the operational perspective, it could be a layering of one challenge onto another.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: We should ensure that the welfare of the clients in these social residential homes will remain the top priority, even as social service agencies convert and adjust to the requirements of the new regime.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: About 10 years ago, when I was the managing director of Community Chest in NCSS, I remember being invited by MSF colleagues then to visit a social residential home run by a charitable social service agency, looking after young children who had experienced severe abuses, including verbal, physical and sexual transgressions committed against them.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: I was carefully prepared by MSF for the visit, so as not to be shocked by behaviours, such as punching fists in the walls and others, before I was brought to visit the Home, as MSF colleagues wanted to discuss fundraising required to improve the care model of these children.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: While I was prepared for the worst, what greeted me at the Home – specifically in a room where some of the children were having tuition for their homework – were innocent young faces, not unlike that of my own son who was about the same age as these children then.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: All I could conclude from that visit was that these children were born in the wrong families and wrong homes.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: What I was thankful for after the visit was an anonymous donor, whom I still do not know the identity of, who eventually donated half a million dollars to Community Chest through a former NCSS Board member and helped MSF pilot a better care model for these children.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: A strong legislative framework and rules to safeguard their living are thus extremely important and necessary.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: I strongly support the Bill, but will like to raise three areas for clarifications and suggestions.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: I have seen VCF alleviate the standards and capabilities of many social service agencies delivering strategic and critical programmes over more than a decade of serving in the social service sector in my work at NCSS.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: The social service agencies like Metta Welfare Association (Metta), Movement for the Intellectually Disabled of Singapore (MINDS), Thye Hua Kwan, St Andrew's, Asian Women Welfare Association (AWWA), TOUCH, Pertapis and Trybe, just to name a few, running social residential homes will know well that these Homes are some of the hardest programmes that they need to deliver among their range of social service programmes that they provide.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: Helping them build standards, staff competencies and operational capabilities should not be a one-off effort but a long-term commitment.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: Another help that MSF and NCSS should seriously consider is the facilitation for better use of public funds to help these social service agencies, such as in the bulk procurement for common equipment like CCTV systems, which can be very costly if each Home procures on its own.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: Next, on clarifying responsibilities of board members and volunteers.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: I note that the Bill provides for powers for MSF to issue Codes of Practices to codify standards of care, including governance, management of premises, resident management and incident management in the Homes.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: Breach of these Codes of Practices may result in regulatory actions for all social residential homes, irrespective of whether they are funded by MSF or not.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: The Bill also provides for comprehensive framework to deter errant operators, where MSF may take regulatory actions and pursue criminal penalties against errant and/or failing social residential homes operators.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: MSF may also issue step-in orders to temporarily take over a failing operator's social residential home to ensure continuity of care.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: While I appreciate the good intentions to safeguard residents and the running such Homes through these changes, I would like to clarify at what level in MSF will the Codes of Practices, that can be issued from time to time with regulatory penalties for non-compliance, be approved.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: I understand that such codes may contain more details and requirements on operators than what the Bill has shown.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: Again, how does MSF strike a balance, considering the capabilities of the operators, and how will potential penalties for breaches be informed to the operators in each Code issued?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: I know of several friends in busy professions who are serving voluntarily on the Boards of the social service agencies running some of these social residential homes out of care and concerns for these vulnerable residents.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: They are unsure how the stiffer regulatory penalties will be imposed on the Board members, individually or collectively, in situations of breaches that are not of their doing.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: They asked what are the implications on the Board, the management and the staff, and how will MSF assess where the buck stops.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: Lastly, on long-term capacity and capability building, I cannot empathise more with the challenges that the social service agencies running these homes face in manpower recruitment, retention and development.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: Many of them are highly reliant on foreign staff as it is difficult to get Singaporeans to work in many of the roles needed to run such Homes.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: From my visits of some of these Homes over the years that I worked in NCSS, I have seen the most vulnerable of vulnerable Singaporeans living in them.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: Many of them, children and seniors included, may not be able to articulate their needs, given their disabilities or trauma that they have experienced unless a responsible adult visits them regularly and is observant of their behaviours and moods.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: Each of the 61 Homes need good Singaporeans who are more privileged to be their volunteers, to serve on their Boards of Visitors and to be donors, like the anonymous donor that I mentioned, who had given to the Community Chest, in my opening paragraph.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: When the homes of our most vulnerable of the vulnerable Singaporeans, the least, the last and the lost are much like better homes that most Singaporeans experience through the decades as Singapore matures as a highly developed nation.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: I think then, we can truly be proud to bear the hallmark of a strong and caring nation who leaves no one behind.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The Social Residential Homes Bill is about care, dignity and responsibility.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It is about how we treat the most vulnerable amongst us – our children, seniors, disabled – those who, for whatever reason, cannot care for themselves.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Some of these individuals have loving families who simply do not have the means or ability to provide round-the-clock care.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Others have no one – no family, no safety net, no place to call home, except for these social residential homes.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Their well-being, their safety, their quality of life, all of it rests on the people who run and work in these facilities.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And it is our duty to make sure that responsibility is met – not just with good intentions, but with real, enforceable standards that ensure quality care.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: But the real question before us today is this: are we setting the highest possible standards?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And more importantly, are we making sure that those standards are upheld every single day, for every single resident?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: First, Mr Speaker, Sir, we all know that Singapore is ageing.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: But let us be clear – this is only useful, if these homes are accessible to the intended users.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What is the plan to ensure that we have enough Homes to meet the growing demand in the next decade?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Have we mapped out where these Homes are needed most?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Are they evenly distributed, or are we going to see some areas well-served while others are left behind?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Conversely, how do we make sure we are not turning people away because there are simply not enough beds?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We should also be encouraging community and private-sector efforts to fill the gaps.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Could we introduce more incentives for non-profit organisations and businesses to build more Homes where they are needed most?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Because no one – no senior, no vulnerable person – should have to struggle just to find a place to live with dignity.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Why should it be any different in social residential homes, where people need daily assistance with everything, from eating to moving to managing their mental well-being?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We also need to talk about the people who do the work.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Many caregivers in these Homes are foreign workers or volunteers.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They are the ones feeding, bathing and caring for residents.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: But are we making sure that they are properly trained?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And are we providing them with enough support, so they do not burn out?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Because if we do not take care of them, they would not be able to take care of our residents.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We also have to ask: will the Government issue more work passes for this sector to ensure we have enough trained caregivers?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) also relax the local-to-Work Permit holder ratios for this sector?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And we need to start treating it that way.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Third, Mr Speaker, Sir, regulations are only as strong as the enforcement behind them.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This Bill gives the Government the power to revoke the licences of those homes which fail to meet the standards.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: However, nowhere does it say that violations must be made public.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If a home is failing its residents, should not the families have the right to know?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Should not there be a public rating or inspection system, like we have for food establishments, so people can make informed choices?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This Bill allows the Government to take over a failing Home, under section 27, but it does not tell us when that will happen.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: How bad does a home have to be, before action is taken?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Who will take over the day-to-day operations after the takeover?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The Bill also introduces Boards of Visitors to check on homes.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Will they be independent committee members or just Government appointees?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Right now, if a resident or their family has concerns, where do they go?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Should there be a public hotline or an independent mediator to handle grievances fairly and transparently?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Because transparency builds trust, and if we want families to feel safe placing their loved ones in these homes, trust is essential.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Lastly, Mr Speaker, Sir, at its core, this Bill is about people.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Residents should have a voice in how these Homes are run.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Could we establish feedback channels so that they can participate in decisions that affect their daily lives?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This Bill also restricts the publication of information about residents under section 38, and while privacy is important, does this mean whistle-blowers cannot report poor conditions?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And can we go a step further and introduce a Residents’ Bill of Rights, like some other countries have, to guarantee dignity, choice and respect for every resident?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Consequently, a social residential home should not just be a place to stay.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: It should be a place to live with dignity.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Because the true strength of our society is not found in how far the most successful can go, but in how well we care for those who struggle, those who are vulnerable and those who are left behind.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Right now, across Singapore, there are seniors, persons with disabilities and individuals without families who depend on social residential homes for their well-being.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They are not just names in a system.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They are our mothers and fathers, our sisters and brothers.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Some of them are even workers who built this nation, who spent their years caring for others, contributing to society.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And now, the question before us is – are we doing enough to care for them?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: But let us be honest, a licence alone does not build a caring home.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We need real mental health support for caregivers because care must go beyond just physical needs.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And we must value and support our caregivers because if we do not care for them, they will not be able to care for our loved ones.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If a home is failing, families deserve to know.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And fourth, we must protect the dignity and rights of residents.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: No one should feel like they have lost their freedom or their voice just because they need care.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: No one should feel like they are trapped in an institution when they should feel at home.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This is not just about passing a Bill.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: If we say we want to build an inclusive, caring and just society, then we have to mean it.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Not just economic growth, but ensuring every Singaporean matters, every Singaporean has dignity and every Singaporean belongs.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Because in Singapore, we do not leave people behind.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: One day, when history looks back at this moment, we would not be judged by the regulations we wrote but by the lives we touched, the dignity we restored and the care we gave.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have three points of clarifications to raise.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My first clarification is on the approval required to deploy individuals to carry out certain prescribed duties.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: During the public consultation on the Bill, respondents expressed concerns about reduced autonomy and potential hiring delays.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: MSF responded that it will work closely with the social residential homes to streamline the approval process and partner the social residential homes in recruitment planning.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Given that the social residential homes often already face manpower challenges from high staff turnover, the new requirement for pre-approval may further constrain the social residential homes already limited manpower resources.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Senior Parliamentary Secretary share the duties that are likely to require pre-approval for deployment?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Senior Parliamentary Secretary share the likely timeframe for such pre-approval?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Senior Parliamentary Secretary also share more details on the approval process and how it will support the social residential homes in recruitment planning?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The step-in arrangements may include appointing another individual to be the person-in-charge of the social residential home, appointing another licensee to operate the social residential home or transferring residents to another social residential home.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These are exceptional powers that should be used as a last resort.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Senior Parliamentary Secretary share whether MSF will have a framework for deciding when the step-in powers will be exercised and which arrangements will be ordered?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For step-in arrangements involving another licensee, can MSF also share how it will prepare another licensee to take over the operations or residents of another social residential home?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is especially given that many social residential homes may not be operating with significant spare capacity.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For instance, will there be a process for MSF to gradually prepare other social residential homes to support step-in arrangements where an social residential home operator appears unable or unwilling to comply with regulatory actions?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: My final clarification is on whistle-blowing protections under the Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It also provides that the identity of the person is protected from disclosure in proceedings.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, a person who suspects an offence relating to a social residential home may not necessarily have access to or make the report to an inspecting officer.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: An informer may instead make the report to a Police officer or any other MSF officer.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Under the Prevention of Corruption Act, as long as the complaint relates to an offence under the Prevention of Corruption Act, the identity of the informer is protected.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It does not matter whether the report was made to the Police or the Corrupt Practices Investigation Bureau.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Senior Parliamentary Secretary clarify whether an individual who reports an offence under the Bill to the Police will be similarly protected by the whistle-blowing protections under section 53?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If not, what is the rationale for limiting the protection to individuals who make the report specifically to an inspecting officer?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Notwithstanding these clarifications, Sir, I stand in support of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked why MSF does not stipulate minimum staffing ratios for Homes in the Bill.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Mr Melvin Yong also asked about the evolution of sector standards over the years.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: As mentioned in my opening speech, we have enhanced our care models.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: In addition to Children’s Homes, Adult Disability Homes, Sheltered Homes and Welfare Homes have also adopted a tiered approach to provide more intensive care and targeted support to residents with higher care needs.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: As the sector continues to grow, our standards of care will also evolve to meet changing needs.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Mr Louis Ng asked about the types of duties carried out by individuals who require MSF’s approval prior to deployment in the Home.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Broadly, these duties would include first, those relating to the overall governance, leadership and management of the Home, such as management of the Home’s financial accounts.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We want to be sure that any individual who takes on any leadership or management responsibilities, such as key appointment holders and person-in-charge, is of good standing.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Second, those involving direct unsupervised contact with residents, such as helping residents who are less mobile with their personal hygiene and meals.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: This is so that we do not place vulnerable residents at undue risk of harm through exposure to individuals with a record of egregious offences.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Mr Ng also asked how long the pre-approval would take and also, support for Homes with recruitment planning.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Concurrently, MSF is reviewing ways to complete the process even faster, including through streamlining or automating some parts of the suitability assessment processes.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling asked about the accuracy of background checks on foreign staff.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Under this Bill, all prospective foreign staff in licensed Homes will be required to submit a self-declaration if they had committed any offence in any country, as specified by MOM.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: If we find out that a false declaration had been made, the individual may be liable to regulatory actions under the Bill, such as cancellation of approval to work in the Home, and/or prosecution under the Penal Code.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Mr Yong asked about the number of cases of Home staff that were investigated and taken to task for excessive use of force.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Several were not substantiated, and where substantiated, staff were taken to task.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: MSF adopts a zero-tolerance approach towards the use of excessive force on our residents and will thoroughly investigate these allegations.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Mr Yip suggested creating a public rating system for Homes, so that family members and the public will be made aware if a Home is performing poorly.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: To address the Member’s underlying concern on accountability, MSF works closely with Homes in the case of incidents to ensure that residents and their family members are aware of the situation, what is being done to address the concerns and to involve them in decisions regarding their care arrangements, where possible.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We will consider practices in other countries to strengthen public accountability.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The goal should be to help the Homes enhance their performance and accountability, and create a culture of continual improvement.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Mr Yip and Mr Yong would also be assured to know that we have multiple channels in place for residents and family members to provide feedback on Homes.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: A Board of Visitors consisting of independent members of the community, such as private and social sector professionals, will visit Homes at least once a quarter.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The Board of Visitors may also visit certain Homes more frequently, if there is a need to monitor them more closely.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: These visits are unannounced to enable the Board of Visitors to check on residents’ living conditions and speak with residents to hear any concerns they may have.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Residents and their family members may also provide their feedback to MSF via our hotline or email.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Through these channels, we can promptly address concerns and foster greater accountability from Homes.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Mr Dennis Tan asked if there were any shortfalls or uneven standards of care across the Homes.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: As mentioned in my opening speech earlier, MSF introduced this Bill to codify the good progress that has been made in raising the quality of care over the years.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: It is not in response to uneven standards of care or any incidents of a serious nature.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Mr Yong raised a few questions on the Singapore Boys’ Home and Singapore Girls’ Home.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: In particular, the reasons for excluding them from this Bill, whether these Homes are subjected to the same standards in this Bill and who is responsible for ensuring the quality of care in these Homes.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The Singapore Boys’ Home and the Singapore Girls’ Home are operated by the Government and are excluded from the licensing regime under this Bill.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: However, this does not mean that they do not need to meet the standards of care.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: In fact, they are held to the same standards, if not higher.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: To ensure good quality care is provided in the Singapore Boys’ Home and Singapore Girls’ Home, these Homes are subjected to independent inspections, as well as regular visits by a Review Board.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Similar to the Board of Visitors, the Review Board comprises independent members of the community, who review the living standards and standards of care in these Homes.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Next, I will address the queries raised on the enforcement framework against errant operators.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Mr Louis Ng and Mr Yip Hon Weng asked if MSF will have a framework to decide when the step-in powers will be exercised and which arrangements will be ordered.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I wish to emphasise that these step-in powers are meant to be a measure of last resort, after all other avenues are exhausted.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Accordingly, the use of step-in powers will cease once the operations of the affected home have stabilised and we are assured of the residents' safety and wellbeing.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: MSF, the affected home as well as the incoming home operator worked closely to ensure a smooth transition for staff and continuity of care for residents.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Mr Ng and Mr Yong also asked how MSF would prepare other licensed homes to take over the operations or residents of a failing home.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: MSF will work closely with both the incoming and outgoing operators to facilitate the handover processes, including the care arrangements for residents during the step-in period.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We will also ensure that capacity is sufficient.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Our priority is to ensure that the continuity of care for residents in the affected home is assured.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: To be clear, activating another licensed home to step-in is only one option that MSF may take under step-in powers.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Other options, include appointing a third-party to advise the licensee on the home's operations or revoking the appointment of an existing key appointment holder and reappointing another individual to take over the responsibilities.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Mr Ng asked whether whistle-blowing protections under clause 53 apply to individuals who report offences under the Bill to the Police.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Mr Yip asked if whistle-blowers would be constrained in reporting poor living or care conditions because of the restriction on publishing information about residents.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Clause 38 protects the identities of residents in these homes from being published or broadcasted.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Whistle-blowers come to MSF to share information privately rather than broadcast identifiable details of clients in the public sphere.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: In addition, under clause 53(2) of the Bill on whistle-blowing, a person who whistle-blows to MSF in good faith cannot be held in any legal proceedings with respect to any restriction on disclosure imposed by any rule of law.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Such a provision was included in our Bill precisely to encourage whistle-blowers to step forward if they have such concerns.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling raised several questions on the level of approval for the Codes of Practice, calibration of penalties for breaches of Codes of Practice and the lines of accountability for regulatory breaches.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: First, the Codes of Practice that are issued to homes are approved by the Director-General.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Second, the type of regulatory action taken will be calibrated, depending on factors, such as degree of harm caused and if it is a repeated breach by the home.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: In some cases, we may suspend approval of specific individuals working in the home.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: In others, we may shorten a home's licence while giving the home guidance on issues that need to be rectified.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Third, in deciding who to take regulatory actions on, please be assured that we have every intention to be fair and reasonable.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We will not be overly punitive to our stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Allow me to illustrate with a hypothetical example.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We intend to introduce a regulatory requirement on the licensee to ensure that staff are adequately trained.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: If a staff member of the home fails to meet the minimum first aid training requirements and is, thus, unable to promptly attend to residents' need for first aid, we may take action against the licensee.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Mr Yong expressed concern that the enhanced penalties may be excessive and could inadvertently discourage operators or staff from joining the sector.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: One notable example is the Healthcare Services Act, which licenses the provision of nursing home service.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Much like our homes, residents in nursing homes are vulnerable and reliant on the home for 24/7 care.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The safety and well-being of our homes' residents are no less important.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We recognise that some homes may be anxious about the enhanced penalties.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: To provide the various stakeholder groups, such as board members, with greater clarity about their duties, we will set out their roles and responsibilities in the Subsidiary Legislation and Codes of Practice.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We will not be punitive from the outset.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Instead, we will work closely with homes to ensure that they are well-supported to meet the regulatory requirements under this Bill.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Next, I will move on to questions and suggestions pertaining to capability building for our homes.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
