text: Mr Melvin Yong and Mr Dennis Tan asked about the regulatory costs arising from this Bill and the support to homes to transit to the new licensing regime.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We do not expect the regulatory costs to be significantly higher than today, as the requirements build upon existing legislation and service requirements that homes are familiar with.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Funding will be customised based on the needs of each home.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: In addition to the one-off Transition Support Package, Ms Ng and Mr Yong suggested setting up a long-term capability building fund to support homes in building up their operational capabilities and staff competencies.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Investing in sector capabilities is one of our key priorities and we have several schemes and grants available to help social service agencies level up.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: NCSS administers the Transformation Sustainability Scheme that provides funding to social service agencies to enhance their strategic and organisational capabilities.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: With this funding, social service agencies are supported in improving staff retention, strengthening volunteer engagement and thereafter, successfully delivering on other capability-building projects.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The Charities Capability Fund, formerly known as VCF that Ms Ng mentioned, continues to be available to social service agencies.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: It covers a range of capability building matters, including governance and management training for charities' board members and staff.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Ms Ng suggested exploring bulk procurement of common equipment to optimise public funds and resources available to the homes.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: MSF and NCSS will work with social service agencies to optimise resource utilisation and adopt solutions that would best meet their needs.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Mr Yip and Mr Yong asked if staff in our homes are paid fairly and are sufficiently supported to ensure that they do not burn out while caring for residents.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Mr Dennis Tan asked a related question about how we intend to support homes' manpower needs.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We are invested in the manpower sustainability of this sector.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: In my Opening speech, I shared about our reviews of the Skills and Salary Guidelines to ensure that staff are paid competitively and about NCSS working closely with social service agencies to develop stronger organisational capabilities and a supportive workplace environment.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Through this pilot, we hope to enhance the value proposition of a career in the sector, specifically, by improving the working conditions and supporting the career development of care staff.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Mr Yip also asked about the support that MSF provides to ensure that homes have sufficient trained caregivers, including those from foreign countries, and whether foreign worker ratios need to be relaxed.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: To this end, MSF will continue to work with MOM to ensure that homes have sufficient work pass quota and flexibility to recruit foreign care staff whilst also ensuring opportunities for local staff to progress in their careers.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Mr Yip spoke about the need for adequate capacity.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: MSF keeps a close eye on the demand and supply of the capacity of our homes.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: For Adult Disability Homes, which includes Adult Disability Hostels, we are actively addressing waitlist management through several initiatives.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We are expanding capacity by adding new facilities and are optimising placement processes to ensure cases with urgent needs are prioritised.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Additionally, we are strengthening community-based support services to provide alternatives to residential care, where appropriate.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We will continue to ensure sufficient capacity to meet projected demand over the long term, an issue that Mr Yong also spoke about.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: As caregivers age and with shrinking family sizes, we expect a slight increase in demand over the next decade.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: At the same time, MSF and the Ministry of Health are ramping up our support for persons with disabilities and seniors to age in place and for those in homes to be reintegrated more quickly back to the community so that fewer of them need to stay in institutional care.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: With the slight increase in demand, manpower needs will also increase.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We will continue to invest in technology and process redesign to enhance workforce productivity.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Relatedly, Mr Yip noted that the Bill empowers the Director-General to set capacity limits on homes and expressed concern that this could lead to turning residents in need away.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: To be clear, the key objective of setting capacity limits is to ensure that quality care can be provided to residents.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: These limits are determined based on practical considerations, which include, physical space requirements, infrastructure capabilities and staffing ratios.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: As I had mentioned earlier, MSF will continue to monitor demand and supply trends to ensure sufficient capacity.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Mr Tan asked why the Bill would need to provide for the possibility of housing different client types or profiles together.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We will work closely with the sector to co-create the future of social residential homes.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Earlier, Ms Ng expressed her appreciation to the individuals who have readily volunteered to be members of the Board of Visitors.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I echo Ms Ng's appreciation for Board of Visitors volunteers and would like to share the example of one such volunteer.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: She is a veteran special educator with over 30 years of experience working with children and adults with developmental needs.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: As the Vice Chairperson of one of our Boards of Visitors, Ms Sharifah used her expertise to provide valuable insights to homes on how they can improve the care they provide to residents.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Volunteers like Ms Sharifah play a pivotal role in ensuring that good quality care is provided to residents.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The Board of Visitors had alerted the management team to feedback from residents on the lack of variety in meals.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: The close partnership between homes, Boards of Visitors and MSF ensures that residents' voices are heard, a point that Mr Yip earlier alluded to with his suggestion for a separate Residents' Bill of Rights to engender dignity, choice and respect for residents.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Many of us may not be familiar with the work that these homes do and the residents that they care for.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: This is because the majority of our 4,000 residents live in the homes 24/7.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Social workers are another key group that play an important role in journeying with the resident through the challenges and milestones in life.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Many of the residents have no one else in their lives to advocate for their needs and to ensure they have access to various resources and opportunities, except for these staff.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: To be clear, the work that the home staff do is tough.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Under their care, residents are given the help they need to facilitate their recovery, to preserve their health and cognitive functions and be meaningfully engaged.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Residents with the potential to live independently or return to their families are also equipped with relevant independent living skills, such as personal care, household chores, budgeting, money management, social skills and help-seeking skills.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: This ensures that residents are set up for success when they are reintegrated back into society.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I want to share the story of Beatrice, a resident of Thuja Home at Pelangi Village.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Beatrice was admitted into the Welfare Home in December 2019 with schizophrenia.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Over the years, staff in Thuja Home worked closely with Beatrice in various areas.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: This includes regular check-ins as well as referrals for psychoeducation and employment.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: With their care and guidance, Beatrice succeeded in securing employment.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Today, she has secured a Housing and Development Board rental flat and will soon be discharged from the home.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: To the staff in our homes, thank you for all that you do.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Your dedication to uplifting the lives of those in need is the reason why residents, like Beatrice, can rebuild their lives, regain independence and step into the future filled with hope.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I believe this Bill is a much-needed step as we strive to uphold the good quality of care provided to residents across the sector and ensure that every single resident is kept safe and well in our homes.

text: Are there any clarifications for the Senior Minister of State Eric Chua?
